title: Stonehaven - Director of Credit & Collateral Risk
description:
Description
At Ledgebrook , we’re building a next-generation insurance infrastructure - fast, smart, and scalable - and are looking for a Director of Credit & Collateral Risk to protect the balance sheet of Stonehaven Specialty Insurance Company, Ledgebrook ’s new third-party hybrid fronting carrier.
This role reports to the Chief Risk Officer and provides independent credit review of every counterparty Stonehaven relies on. It works closely with Finance, Legal, the Director of Ceded Reinsurance, and the program teams, and approves counterparties independently of the people who negotiate with them.
About the Role
Stonehaven is seeking a Director of Credit & Collateral Risk to independently approve, monitor, and secure every counterparty on its balance sheet, from reinsurers and captives to MGAs, TPAs, and banks. The successful candidate will be a seasoned credit risk professional with hands-on command of letters of credit, reinsurance trusts, and collateral sizing, a track record of enforcing concentration limits and running watch-list governance, and the independence and judgment to decline a counterparty regardless of the program attached to it.
﻿What You'll Do:

• Maintain the Third-Party Credit Risk Policy for the Chief Risk Officer, including credit standards by counterparty type, reinsurer credit tiers, concentration limits, and the exception process.

• Perform independent due diligence and credit approval for reinsurers, captives, MGAs, TPAs, banks, premium finance companies, and surplus lines brokers before Stonehaven engages them, including reinsurers that arrive attached to a program.

• Independently verify all collateral, confirming letters of credit directly with issuing banks and trust assets directly with trustees, never relying on counterparty-supplied documents alone.

• Size collateral for each collateralized reinsurer and captive, compare required and posted collateral monthly, and issue and escalate top-up demands when collateral falls short.

• Monitor the credit quality of letter-of-credit issuing banks and ensure every letter of credit comes from an eligible institution.

• Enforce hard concentration limits per reinsurer, reinsurer group, collateral provider, and bank, and in aggregate across all programs.

• Build and maintain the counterparty credit risk register, the collateral register, and the aggregate credit exposure dashboard with Finance and Technology.

• Run ongoing monitoring of rating alerts, financial statements obtained from independent sources, recoverable aging, MGA premium trust accounts, and TPA loss funds.

• Manage the Watch List, including placement triggers, required actions, exit plans, and Board notification.

• Design and run the credit stress scenarios used in ORSA, including reinsurer default, simultaneous downgrades, letter-of-credit bank failure, and MGA or TPA insolvency.

• Present counterparty, collateral, and concentration status to the Reinsurance Security and Risk & Capital Committees, and support Finance on Schedule F, RBC credit risk, and Form F disclosures.

• Review material contracts with Legal through a credit lens, including offset rights, collateral triggers, security interests, and termination for financial cause.

Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events
Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them
Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading
Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise
Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About Wellio

It's probably not news to you that wellbeing and mental health issues are rising globally. 40% of young people have experienced a mental health disorder in the past year alone, so chances are you know someone who has been affected.

At Wellio , we help schools put wellbeing at the heart of every student’s school experience. We believe improving youth mental health is one of the most important challenges of our time.

Wellio is building the world’s first Wellbeing Management System , bringing the best of student wellbeing practice into one simple platform. We help schools teach wellbeing consistently, identify students who may be struggling earlier, coordinate support and continuously improve student outcomes.

And it’s working.

Today, Wellio powers wellbeing programs in 1,000 schools across 25 countries , supporting millions of students. We’re on track to complete our fourth consecutive year of 100% growth , and we’re just getting started.

It shouldn’t matter which school you attend, or what country you live in. Every student should have access to the best tools and support to thrive. Our mission is big and important, and that’s why we’re looking for the very best people to help us achieve it.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Senior Product Designer to be the designer on one of our product squads. At Wellio , product design is one role, not three. Our designers do the research, help shape the bet, design the flows and interfaces, and then build them. Design owns the design system in the app, and alongside Figma, the codebase is now where a lot of our design happens. Our new student avatar builder went from idea to shipped in three days, built end to end by our designer with AI. Before AI, we’d have budgeted three weeks for it. We run Shape Up, with six-week build cycles and small squads where a PM, designer, engineers and content people own one outcome for schools together.

It’s a rare chance to help define how great design gets done with AI, while building tools that improve millions of young lives

What you will do

You’ll work day to day with your squad’s PM and engineers to take features from shaping to shipped, owning the design process end to end.

Design and build

• Design complete experiences, from fat marker sketches to pixel-perfect interfaces

• Build your designs in the codebase with AI and ship front-end changes without a handoff

• Check your code with our AI review skills, then pair with engineers through code review and on technical constraints

• Contribute patterns to a design system that scales across the platform

Design with AI

• Give AI the context, components and constraints to build things that look and work like Wellio

• Improve the skills, rules and design system context in our codebase so everyone’s output gets better

• Share what works, and what doesn’t, with the rest of the team

Research and discovery

• Observe teachers and students using the product in real classrooms

• Run user interviews and put working prototypes in front of users before we commit to building

• Use PostHog and session recordings to see where people get stuck

• Turn insights into clear design principles and interface patterns

Content and collaboration

• Write clear interface copy and work with our content team to keep messaging consistent

• Design content-heavy educational interfaces that balance information density with usability

• Shape pitches live with your PM and engineers, and present work at the betting table

• Create materials that help sales and customer success communicate the product’s value

• Mentor others on design thinking and user-centred approaches

title: Staff Software Engineer, Backend
description:
STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, BACKEND

 

ABOUT STREAM

Stream powers real-time Chat https://getstream.io/chat/, Video https://getstream.io/video/, Activity Feeds https://getstream.io/activity-feeds/, and AI Moderation https://getstream.io/moderation/ for more than 1 billion end users across 4,000+ apps, from Strava and Bumble to eBay and Patreon. Our platform processes billions of API requests per month and supports applications with millions of concurrent users, while delivering highly reliable, low-latency services and a great developer experience.

THE ROLE

We’re looking for Staff Software Engineers. You’ll join our Chat or Activity Feeds team and own backend systems that thousands of developers build their products on, from how they’re structured to how they scale.

This is a full-time role based in our Amsterdam (visa & relocation support possible), Toronto, or Skopje office. We are also open to hiring the right person remote from the EU.

ABOUT YOU

You’ve built backend systems at high scale and stayed long enough to live with your own decisions, good and bad. You care about how a system is structured, not only the next feature, and you can explain your trade-offs to the people who’ll live with them. Maybe you led a team for a few years and chose to go back to hands-on work. That’s welcome here: this is an individual contributor role, and you’ll write code and touch databases yourself. Our leads spend about 80% of their time hands-on too. You won’t enjoy it if you want to manage people, or if you’d rather stay away from infrastructure and database work.

We’re also hiring Senior Engineers on these teams. If your experience fits Senior better than Staff, we’ll say so openly and talk it through with you.

YOU HAVE

- Extensive backend engineering experience, including technical leadership on systems in production.

- Proficiency in Go, Python, or in another backend language plus the willingness to switch to Go.

- Experience building features used by a large number of users, and scaling them as usage grows.

- Strong experience with a relational database. We use PostgreSQL, but any relational database counts.

- Hands-on experience with Redis or a similar in-memory data store.

- Experience building public APIs or SDKs that other developers use.

- Comfort with infrastructure and database work as part of your normal week, including Kubernetes.

- Good written and spoken English. It’s our working language.

BONUS POINTS

- PostgreSQL in production at scale, including sharding, partitioning or large migrations.

- Experience improving or redesigning legacy parts of a system that’s serving live traffic.

- Go and gRPC in production at high request rates.

- Messaging, feeds or other real-time systems, or message queues such as RabbitMQ or Kafka.

- Distributed storage internals, such as Raft or RocksDB.

- You’ve cut infrastructure cost at a company where margins mattered.

- Experience running workloads on GCP or AWS.

Don’t worry if you haven’t used every tool we run. You’ll get exposure to most of them, and you’re welcome to convince us to add your favorites.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE EXCITING

- Scale: more than 1 billion end users and billions of API requests a month go through the systems you’ll own.

- Impact: cost per message and query latency show up directly in our margins and in the apps of customers like Strava and Patreon.

- Stack: Go, gRPC, RocksDB and Python; PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ; GCP and Kubernetes; Grafana, Prometheus, ELK (Elasticsearch and Kibana), Jaeger and Tempo for distributed tracing, and Datadog; Redis, Valkey and Memcached.

- Starting point: you’ll ship to production in your first weeks and own a meaningful area within your first months.

WHAT WE OFFER

- Generous compensation

- Stock options

Amsterdam office benefits:

- 28 days paid time off plus Dutch public holidays.

- Pension plan with a company contribution.

- NS Business Card or a company bike, covered by Stream.

- EUR 500 per year for pers

title: Head of Enablement
description:
Description
We have the category, the product, and a GTM team hiring fast. What we lack is the thing that makes every new AE, SE, CSM, and BDR as effective as our best one inside their first quarter instead of their third.
You'll be Reco 's first enablement leader, owning the full lifecycle from the first discovery call through technical validation, adoption, renewal, and expansion. Sales and CS sit together deliberately: in a land-and-expand security business, the story a rep tells in the deal and the value a CSM proves in month six have to match. You'll build it hands-on before you build a team.
Responsibilities
1. Programmatic - get knowledge out of people's heads

• Extract what isn't written down: our founders' framing of the category, the SE's instinct for which POV will convert, the CSM who knows why a customer expanded.

• Run the mechanics: win/loss debriefs, deal teardowns, call library curation, ride-alongs, SME interviews across Product, Research, and the Office of the CTO.

• Turn raw input into structured, versioned, findable content with named owners and refresh cadences, so nothing quietly goes stale.

2. Technical - product depth

• Take the field past feature lists: how Reco works, why the architecture matters to a CISO, and what shipping new app coverage in days means competitively.

• Own demo certification and hands-on labs. Nobody demos solo until they pass a live bar.

• Enabling the surrounding landscape reps must speak to: SaaS and identity architecture, OAuth and integration risk, AI agent and MCP exposure, compliance frameworks.

• Ship field readiness with every release.

3. Sales and go-to-market

• Build the core playbook: persona-based discovery for CISOs, security architects, and IT owners; qualification; multi-threading; objection handling; close.

• Make MEDDPICC the discipline behind how reps qualify and how the forecast gets built, not a CRM field. Coach managers to it.

• Own the POV playbook end to end - entry criteria, agreed success criteria, milestones, exit criteria, handoff to close. Kill the POVs that shouldn't have started.

• Own commercial enablement: pricing and packaging, business case, deal structure, margin, discounting discipline with Finance and RevOps, and negotiation.

• Own competitive enablement for SSPM and AI security. Battlecards current within days of a market move.

Onboarding, CS, and coaching

• Role-based onboarding with 30/60/90 certification gates that mean something: recorded pitch, live discovery sim, demo pass, customer value review.

• Post-sale plays: time-to-value, adoption milestones, EBRs, renewal defense, and expansion tied to new app coverage and AI agent security. Train CSMs to have commercial conversations.

• Coach from real calls, not course completions. Equip frontline managers for weekly 1:1s, pipeline reviews, and deal inspections.

• Own the enablement stack, instrument the function, and work AI-first to personalize paths and scale coaching.

Requirements

• 8+ years in GTM or revenue enablement, including building a function from zero at a high-growth B2B SaaS company.

• You've enabled both sides - AEs, SEs, BDRs, and CSMs.

• Technical enough to sit in a POV without a translator. Fluency in SaaS and identity architecture, cloud security, and AI/agentic risk. Security background strongly preferred.

• You've walked into an org where the expertise sat in a few heads and left behind a maintained body of content. You can interview a principal engineer and come out with a value prop a rep can use that afternoon.

• You've made MEDDPICC (or Command of the Message, Challenger) actually change rep behavior.

• Comfortable owning pricing, business case, discounting, and negotiation enablement.

• Metrics-driven and a strong program manager: baselines, named owners, real timelines, follow-through.

• A builder, not an administrator. You measure your work in deals progressed.

title: Technical Founder
description:
Technical Co-founder / Founding Tech Lead
Europe · Remote + on-site in the Netherlands · Start alongside your current work · Milestone-based equity

99 agents. One co-founder missing.

There’s never been a better time to build. But building something is getting easier for everyone.

The interesting question: what makes it worth building and hard to copy?

Our conviction: data is the ultimate anti-commodity. Unique, useful data should be at the heart of every proposition we pursue.

We're looking for a technical founder who gets excited about that. Someone to spot opportunities with me, challenge them, build them, and turn the strongest into businesses.

What we’re getting into

We’ll explore customer problems within my network, select two propositions, and work towards product-market fit.

You bring the technical depth and the urge to make things happen. We figure out the business together.

Global ambition, a European base, and an eye on what we can learn from US speed, Chinese coordination, and Europe’s collective strengths.

You’ll probably enjoy this if…

- You think about the customer before the stack. Who has this problem? How painful is it? Will they pay? Then: how do we solve it?

- You’re already building. Show us something people use and tell us what you personally made happen.

- You use AI throughout your work. Our ambition is to spend 80% of our time on creativity, strategy, people, and delivery, with AI handling as much of the rest as possible.

- You ship, learn, and ship again. A customer using an imperfect solution teaches us something. Another month of polishing assumptions doesn’t.

- You can own the difficult bits. Infrastructure, security, data quality, permissions, reliability. AI can help; the judgment is yours.

- You don’t wait for a backlog. You can talk to a customer, identify the problem, and decide what to try next.

- You stay with the outcome. When something breaks or a customer gets stuck, you help get it sorted. You care what happens after deployment.

You should be comfortable moving between a customer conversation, a product decision, and a production issue. That’s the work.

The practical part

You must be based in Europe and able to work together in the Netherlands regularly. We’ll combine remote work with in-person sessions.

We’ll start alongside our current activities until we find product-market fit, with a clear weekly commitment agreed upfront. Bring urgency, follow-through, and room in your life to build.

Remuneration starts with milestone-based equity, with milestones and ownership terms agreed before we begin. Cash compensation follows once revenue supports it.

Skip the polished cover letter. Show me something.

Apply with three short answers and take the AI intake (rubric + interview, appr 15-20 min):

1. What have you shipped? Share a link or demo, your contribution, and what happened when people used it.

2. Where do you see a customer problem with a data advantage worth building around?

3. Where are you based, how much time can you commit, and can you work together in the Netherlands?

Warm introductions from people who know your work are welcome. Please apply through this page so everything lands in one place.

If you’ve been looking for someone to build with, let’s see what we can make happen.

title: Software Engineer - AI Tooling Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Software Engineer, AI Tooling Infrastructure to join our AI Tooling team and help build and run the backend services behind Supabase’s AI products. The Supabase MCP server is one example of what the team runs in production, alongside the services that support agent skills and the dashboard assistant. You’ll work closely with the Platform, SRE, Auth, Billing and Edge Functions teams, and with the engineers on the AI Tooling team who build the product surfaces.

The AI Tooling team runs its own services in production and carries its own on-call. Traffic from AI clients and agents behaves differently from traffic from people: hundreds of calls a minute, retry loops, and no reading of deprecation warnings. This role makes sure the services they use are reliable, correctly authorized and observable. It is a systems and infrastructure role rather than a product AI role, and it is not an SRE role. You will build and operate these systems, not only advise on them.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments, owns what they ship in production, and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

In this role, you’ll:

- Build and operate the production backend services behind Supabase’s AI products, including the MCP server: deployment, scaling, configuration and release.

- Take ownership of how those services are structured, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

- Define, measure and meet reliability targets for the services the team runs. Set SLOs with the SRE team, track error budgets, and use them to decide what to fix first.

- Participate in the AI Tooling team on-call rotation, and be a first responder for incidents in those services. Investigate, fix, coordinate with other teams during incidents, and write the follow-ups and runbooks.

- Work the AI Tooling team support queue alongside on-call, and turn recurring issues into fixes rather than repeated manual answers.

- Own authentication and authorization for AI and agent clients: OAuth apps, scoped tokens, and permissions that make sense for agents as well as humans, including how we change or deprecate a permission without breaking existing integrations.

- Own observability for the services the team runs: metrics, traces, logs, dashboards and alerts, so we find problems before customers do.

- Handle capacity and abuse for agent traffic: rate limits, cost and safety controls, and behavior under load or when a dependency degrades.

- Improve the architecture of the services the team owns as they grow, including splitting or reshaping a service when that makes it safer to run and easier to change.

- Work with the Platform team on shared code, review ownership and release process, and with the SRE team on infrastructure, alerting and incident practice.

- Contribute to the code of the AI Tooling team’s tools, such as the MCP server, where it affects reliability and security, in partnership with the engineers who own the product surface.

YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

Must have:

- Have 5+ years of experience building and running backend services in production, and have carried on-call for them.

- Write strong TypeScript or Go, and are comfortable working in the other.

- Have designed and operated APIs with real consumers: versioning, error handling, rate limiting, and backwards-compatible change.

- Know OAuth, OIDC, JWT and API authorization well enough to debug them in production and to explain where implementations commonly deviate from the spec.

- Have a good understanding of PostgreSQL and relational databases.

title: KIP Spring 2027 - Development Intern - Media Research Center
tags: Part Time or Full Time Internship
description:
The Koch Internship Program (KIP) is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the admissions process early!

About Media Research Center:
 
The Media Research Center (MRC) is America’s premier media watchdog. Since 1987, MRC has exposed left-wing bias in news and pop culture, defended free speech, and fought Big Tech censorship of conservatives. With powerful tools like its TV news archive and CensorTrack database, MRC provides hard evidence of bias and censorship. We educate the public and shape the national conversation across platforms that generate over 500 million weekly impressions.
 
About the role 
Are you passionate about protecting free speech and calling out censorship in the digital age? The Media Research Center is seeking a Free Speech America Intern to join the team working to expose Big Tech’s suppression of conservative voices. As an intern, you will help monitor censorship trends across major platforms like Google, Facebook, and X/Twitter, while researching and compiling examples of bias for publication and outreach.
 
This is a hands-on opportunity for students and recent graduates who want to be part of the fight to hold Big Tech accountable and inform the public about the growing threat to online expression.
 
This internship is designed for students and recent graduates. The position is in-person only at MRC headquarters; remote work is not available.
 

Stand Together Fellowships believes that diversity in experiences, perspectives, knowledge and ideas fuels creativity, broadens knowledge, and helps drive success. Our admissions office treats all program participants and applicants with honesty, dignity, respect and sensitivity. We welcome all qualified applicants regardless of color, race, religion, religious creed, sex, gender or gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, ethnicity, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy (including medical needs which may arise from pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), military and veteran status, genetic information, marital or familial status, political affiliation, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances.

title: Principal AI Engineer
description:
Principal AI Engineer
BuzzBoard · Remote (WFH) · Engineering / AI The role
BuzzBoard builds AI products for the B2SMB market - helping agencies, media companies, and sellers understand small businesses and market to them at a level of personalization that wasn't previously economical. Our platform is built on frontier models end to end. Not AI features bolted onto a legacy product - the products are agent systems.
Our products span multi-agent marketing content generation, real-time AI voice intake, and pre- and post-sales intelligence for SMBs - Zylo, IRIS, Ignite, and Ember. They share a common internal pipeline for orchestration, retrieval, tool use, evaluation, and deployment.
This role owns the architecture underneath that pipeline. Not one feature - the shared layer every product depends on: how retrieval is built and measured, how agents reason and hold state and fail safely, which models run where and what happens when one degrades, how output quality is evaluated before it ships, and where the line sits between what a model decides and what deterministic code decides. You'll set that architecture, build the reusable patterns products inherit, guide the engineers implementing them, and own whether it holds up in production at volume.
It's a senior individual-contributor role. Two boundaries, stated plainly:

•
Not a research role. The deliverable is a shipped, reliable capability, not a paper or a demo.

•
Not a DevOps role. You need to be fluent in deployment and able to get a service into production, but full-time platform ownership sits elsewhere. Your center of gravity is AI system design.

If your GenAI experience is mostly notebooks and proofs of concept that never carried real traffic, this is not the role.
What you'll own
AI system architecture. Design the systems behind content generation, business intelligence, recommendations, and agentic workflows - including where the boundary sits between what a model decides and what deterministic code decides. Create reusable patterns, prompts, evaluation flows, and orchestration layers that hold up across products rather than being rebuilt per feature.
Agentic workflows. Lead the design of agents that reason, call tools and APIs, manage state, checkpoint, and hand tasks off cleanly. Build the guardrails that keep them grounded and predictable - the hard part is not making an agent act, it's making it fail safely and legibly when it's wrong.
Retrieval and model strategy. Design RAG pipelines end to end: chunking, embeddings, metadata, reranking, and retrieval evaluation that actually measures whether the right context arrived. Own model selection across ecosystems on the axes that matter - cost, latency, accuracy, reliability - and define the fallback and model-switching behavior for when a provider degrades.
Evaluation and quality. Stand up the evaluation frameworks that decide whether an AI output ships: output quality, edit ratio, hallucination rate, schema adherence, latency, failure rate, inference cost. Build regression testing so a prompt or model change can't silently break production. Turn “the output feels off” into a measured threshold.
Production readiness. Partner with engineering and platform teams so systems are deployable, observable, and maintainable. Package services (Python, FastAPI/Flask, Docker) when it's the fastest path, and diagnose the production failure modes specific to AI - rate limits, cost spikes, model failures, degraded output - rather than escalating them blind.
Technical leadership. Mentor GenAI engineers, review designs and prompts and workflows and evals, and translate product requirements into architecture with measurable acceptance criteria. Communicate the tradeoffs to engineers and to leadership in language each can act on.

title: Data Partnerships Manager (1-year contract)
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

WHY THIS ROLE?

At Cohere, we strive to continually improve our large language models. Academic research and real-world experience has demonstrated that high quality, diverse datasets can contribute as much to the performance and capabilities of LLMs as the underlying model architecture and training regimen. We at Cohere believe data will play a central role in accelerating the advancement of our already world-class language models.

Data is therefore critical to our success. Our ability to acquire data that is accurate, relevant, and timely is key to our ability to improve the quality of our models. We strive to continuously improve our data acquisition processes and systems to ensure that we have the data we need to stay competitive and meet the needs of our customers. We run frequent experiments to learn more about the role of data for model quality, from data mixtures, to cleaning techniques, to quality control.

- Partner with Modeling to manage the relationships and data requirements with external data scraping vendors

- Facilitate hand-off of newly acquired datasets to Modeling and Annotation

- Product manage novel data collection methods and applications as needed

- Always keep an eye towards scaling the function with bespoke processes and tools

- You have more than 3 years of experience managing data vendor programs

- You've worked in a partnership-focused role at an AI-focused company, and have built relationships with AI data suppliers

- You're proficient in data analysis and data management

- You're energized by proactively seeking out new data sources and building long-term, trusting relationships with vendors

- You enjoy cross-functional collaboration and have partnered with Technical and Business teams

- You're resourceful and approach problem-solving creatively

title: Corporate Development Sales Associate
description:
Harris Computer's M&A team is looking for a Corporate Development Sales Associate to join our innovative Team!

We’re looking for a high-energy, resilient sales professional to drive our M&A strategy. As a Corporate Development Sales Associate, you'll be at the forefront of our growth, responsible for identifying, connecting with, and building relationships with software company founders and executives.

If you are a self-starter who thrives on autonomy, is passionate about building a pipeline from scratch, and is motivated by the thrill of initiating conversations that lead to major acquisitions, we want to hear from you!

The remote role is eligible to anyone in the U.S. and Canada.

What your impact will be:

•
Develop the M&A Pipeline: Proactively identify and source software companies that align with our investment goals; Use initiative and outreach strategies to build a robust pipeline of opportunities.

•
Initiate and Build Key Relationships: Lead outbound prospecting through strategic, targeted outreach. You will build rapport with business owners and senior leadership, establishing strong professional connections.

•
Be a Trusted Partner: Develop and nurture long-term relationships with key decisionmakers, building long-term credibility and positioning Harris as the acquirer of choice.

•
Innovate Our Process: Develop and implement new, innovative methods to improve our outreach process, with your contributions being highly visible and valued.

•
Leverage Your Tools: Use our M&A CRM as a strategic tool to manage your pipeline and ensure meticulous tracking of all activities, providing you with the data to make effective decisions.

What we’re looking for:

•
Proactive & Goal-Oriented: You are a self-motivated individual with a track record of taking initiative and achieving targets in a business development environment. You thrive when given the autonomy to manage your own work.

•
Exceptional Relationship Builder: You are energized by interacting with others and possess a natural ability to build trust and rapport. You communicate clearly and effectively with people at all levels, including C-suite executives.

•
Entrepreneurial Drive: You are a high-energy, responsive self-starter who works well independently. You have the tenacity and resilience to see complex outreach campaigns through to success.

•
Executive Presence & Maturity: You can confidently and credibly engage with founders and senior executives, representing Harris with professionalism.

•
Business Acumen: You have a solid understanding of business operations, enabling you to quickly assess opportunities and articulate your ideas with conviction. 2 - 5 years of experience in M&A is preferred.

About Us:
Harris Computer is the largest operating group of Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU), the most effective acquirer of software businesses globally. Harris acquires vertical market software businesses, manages them using industry best practices, and builds them for the future. Through acquisitions, Harris has grown extensively from its roots in the utilities, local government, education, and healthcare sectors. We have completed over 170 software acquisitions in 20+ software sectors, have 190+ offices globally and employ over 10,000 team members within Harris companies.

Salary Range
The hiring range for this role is $65,000 to $80,000 per year. Final compensation will be based on experience, skills, market conditions, and internal equity.

What we offer:

• Plenty of opportunities to grow your career

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits

• 3 weeks of vacation plus 5 personal days to recharge

• Employee stock ownership, RRSP program, 401k + matching

• A chance to give back through community involvement

• Flexible work arrangements to suit your lifestyle

Mais do que validar funcionalidades, buscamos um profissional com visão sistêmica, capaz de atuar desde as fases iniciais dos projetos, participando da análise de requisitos, revisão de especificações, identificação de impactos em processos e sistemas correlatos e definição das estratégias de teste mais adequadas para cada contexto. O desafio envolve garantir a qualidade de soluções que integram um ecossistema complexo de aplicações, exigindo olhar crítico, capacidade analítica e forte interação com equipes multidisciplinares.
Esperamos alguém que seja referência técnica em qualidade, contribuindo para o fortalecimento de boas práticas, melhoria contínua dos processos, disseminação da cultura de qualidade e evolução das estratégias de testes funcionais e não funcionais, incluindo automação, performance, segurança e regressão.
Na sua rotina de trabalho, você vai se deparar com as seguintes atividades:

• Participar desde as fases iniciais dos projetos, contribuindo para a análise de requisitos, especificações funcionais e critérios de aceite.

• Elaborar estratégias, planos, cenários e casos de teste alinhados aos objetivos dos projetos.

• Executar testes funcionais, integrados, regressivos, exploratórios e automatizados.

• Planejar e apoiar a execução de testes não funcionais, como performance, carga, segurança e persistência de dados.

• Validar integrações entre sistemas e garantir a consistência das regras de negócio.

• Registrar, acompanhar e apoiar a resolução de defeitos e não conformidades junto aos times de desenvolvimento.

• Atuar em múltiplos projetos e squads simultaneamente, contribuindo para a qualidade das entregas de forma colaborativa.

• Produzir indicadores, métricas e relatórios de qualidade.

• Promover melhorias contínuas nos processos de desenvolvimento e testes.

• Compartilhar conhecimento e disseminar boas práticas de qualidade, apoiando a evolução técnica dos demais profissionais da área.

title: Account Executive - London
description:
About Us

Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.

Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is built in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Denmark and Finland already love running on Tebi.

About the Role

We're looking for a natural Sales person who is passionate about hospitality. Sales is at the heart of our business growth right now, and you will be driving it forward in your day-to-day. This role is about more than closing deals, it is about blending with the hospitality scene and winning the market.

In your day-to-day you can expect a mix of top of funnel activities, field sales, cold sales, networking, events and more.

What You’ll Do

Our sales are not your typical SaaS or office sales. We meet our customers where they operate:

- Find the coolest new hospitality spots in town that everyone talks about

- Create engaging ways to show our product

- Use creative communication strategies to close the deal that will help the merchant operate smarter

- Do a smooth handover to the onboarding team to make sure we go live quickly and successfully

- Efficiently use our CRM and other Sales tools (Hubspot, Clay, AI) to leave more time for creativity and connection

- Continuously improve and revisit our sales funnel

- Keep an eye on the new developments in the industry and the merchants needs to create our own path

What You’ll Need

You are a natural relationship builder with a passion for hospitality industry:

- Hands-on approach, independence and hunger for fast-paced operations

- Natural curiosity and a healthy appetite for calculated risk - we want you to try new things and not be afraid to fail

- Strong and engaging communication skills - you can grab an attention of a busy hospitality owner and keep them interested

- Passion and curiosity for hospitality and hospitality tech

- A minimum of 3 years of experience in Sales, Commercial Account Management or Hospitality

- Previous POS/ Hospitality tech sales is a strong plus

- You are comfortable working in English

If this speaks to you we can be the right fit. Learn more about how we work from our Recipe here: https://www.tebi.com/gb/careers https://www.tebi.com/gb/careers.

Benefits:

- Start-up Equity

- Competitive Salary

- Flexible time off

- Team events

What is Restaurant Software?

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi

title: Senior Board Test Engineer

About the job

Turn board design insight into reliable tests that detect manufacturing defects in Graphcore’s hardware.

As a Senior Board Test Engineer in Bristol, you’ll develop manufacturing tests for Graphcore’s advanced electronic products. You’ll focus on printed circuit board assemblies and the faults that affect their operation.

Your work will help improve defect coverage across the test and inspection tools used by contract electronics manufacturers. You’ll help the team detect and manage hardware faults arising during manufacturing and product use.

You’ll analyse PCB designs for testability and manufacturing risks, then develop boundary scan and embedded functional tests. You’ll also diagnose complex electronic faults down to component level.

The role takes your test solutions beyond development, through deployment and support in factory and field environments.

The team and culture

The Product Test and Diagnosis team detects and manages hardware defects across chips, boards and finished systems. Its work covers manufacturing sites and products in the field.

You’ll work closely with Hardware Design and Manufacturing Operations, linking design analysis with manufacturing test needs. You’ll also work with software, silicon design and external board test partners on complex hardware problems.

What we’re looking for

• Strong electronics fundamentals and experience in manufacturing test for advanced electronic systems.

• Understanding of PCB manufacturing, surface-mount assembly, failure mechanisms, and automated optical and X-ray inspection capabilities.

• Experience developing JTAG 1149 boundary scan test solutions.

• Awareness of bed-of-nails testing (ICT/MDA) and high-volume in-system or on-bo
